# Mining Engine Checklist: Repository Mining Engine

**Purpose**: Review whether the Repository Mining Engine requirements are complete, clear, consistent, measurable, and ready for implementation.
**Created**: 2026-09-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are snapshot scope intent, valid empty scope, and missing or inaccessible selected entities distinguished with explicit outcomes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003–FR-006]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are the outcomes for partial scope-resolution failures defined separately from repository result counters and without fabricated repository records? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010–FR-011]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are the required RepositoryExecution identity, lifecycle, timing, summary, and safe error fields defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008–FR-009]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are the Repository Summary Rule's factual outputs and the boundary from Findings clearly specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, FR-014]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are execution-level and repository-level read contracts, their ownership relationship, and their safe projections defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020–FR-021; Plan §API and dashboard integration]
- [ ] CHK006 - Are requirements for linking repository results into the existing dashboard clear while preserving the unavailable Findings detail state? [Completeness, Spec §FR-021]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 - Are the aggregation rules unambiguous for empty scope, all successes, mixed repository outcomes, scope failures, and pre-processing failures? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010; Plan §Scope resolution and partial failures]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is the identity used to deduplicate effective repositories clear across explicit selections, overlapping groups, and nested groups? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the meaning of each execution counter clear, including why scope-resolution failures do not inflate `failed_repository_count`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011; Data Model §MiningExecution]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are default-branch selection and the no-default-branch failure outcome explicit and free of guessed branch names? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK011 - Are eligible-file counting, excluded path-segment matching, extension normalization, extensionless names, ordering, and truncation defined precisely enough for consistent results? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014–FR-015; Plan §File policy and Repository Summary Rule]
- [ ] CHK012 - Are the tree-entry limit and behavior at/above the limit clear enough to prevent a partial tree from being reported as a complete summary? [Clarity, Plan §GitLab retrieval strategy]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 - Do the empty-scope success rule and explicit unresolved-scope failure rule remain consistent across acceptance scenarios, functional requirements, success criteria, and aggregation design? [Consistency, Spec §US1, FR-010, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK014 - Do the repository counters reconcile with persisted RepositoryExecution rows while scope failures affect aggregate status through their separate count? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010–FR-011; Data Model §MiningExecution]
- [ ] CHK015 - Are Feature 006 lifecycle ownership and Feature 008's permitted lifecycle extensions consistent, with no arbitrary public status mutation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, FR-009; Plan §Pipeline boundaries]
- [ ] CHK016 - Does completion-meaning wording distinguish actual repository processing from Feature 006's former orchestration-only completion? [Consistency, Plan §API and dashboard integration; API Contract §Execution detail additive fields]
- [ ] CHK017 - Are Feature 009 scheduling and Feature 010 Finding behavior consistently deferred across scope, assumptions, rule output, API, and UI requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, FR-014, FR-021, FR-024]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK018 - Can the measurable outcomes objectively establish uniqueness, counter reconciliation, failure isolation, deterministic summaries, safety, and concurrency bounds? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-008]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are configured concurrency, repository-tree, per-file, page, and extension bounds stated with defaults and validation behavior? [Measurability, Spec §FR-015–FR-016; Plan §Technical Context and §Concurrency]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are API pagination limits, ordering, not-found behavior, and additive response compatibility objectively defined? [Acceptance Criteria, Plan §API and dashboard integration; API Contract §List repository executions]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 - Are direct repository selection, owned-project group hierarchy, nested groups, shared-project exclusion, overlap, and deterministic ordering covered? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004–FR-005; Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK022 - Are missing credentials, credential decryption/validation problems, URL changes, and GitLab instance mismatch covered without allowing requests against the wrong instance? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006–FR-007; Plan §Credential and GitLab instance boundary]
- [ ] CHK023 - Are provider timeout, authorization, not-found, malformed response, pagination failure, and missing default-branch outcomes normalized and safely isolated? [Coverage, Spec §US2 and Edge Cases; Plan §GitLab retrieval strategy]
- [ ] CHK024 - Are crash/interruption and duplicate invocation scenarios addressed without false completion or duplicate repository records? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005, FR-018; Data Model §RepositoryExecution]
- [ ] CHK025 - Are repository-list loading, failure/retry, valid empty scope, pre-processing failure with no rows, and mixed-result states distinguished in the dashboard requirements? [Coverage, Spec §US3; Dashboard Contract §Loading, error, and empty states]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK026 - Are credential, provider-body, exception, database-error, fingerprint, and internal-metadata non-disclosure boundaries consistent across persistence, logs, and APIs? [Security, Spec §FR-007, FR-012; API Contract §Security and compatibility]
- [ ] CHK027 - Are keyboard access, semantic status, accessible loading/error feedback, narrow layouts, and readable long paths specified for repository history? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021; Dashboard Contract §Accessibility and responsiveness]
- [ ] CHK028 - Are PostgreSQL-only constraint/concurrency claims conditioned on PostgreSQL validation, with an explicit response when the database environment is unavailable? [Reliability, Spec §FR-023; Plan §Technical Context]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK029 - Are dependencies on Feature 003 credentials, Feature 004 scope semantics, Feature 006 lifecycle/snapshot, and Feature 007 dashboard identified without substituting mutable current configuration data? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions; Research §Feature 001–007 boundaries]
- [ ] CHK030 - Are GitLab API assumptions about the default branch, recursive tree, and complete pagination supported and bounded for GitLab.com and self-managed instances? [Dependency, Plan §GitLab retrieval strategy; Research §GitLab API choice]
- [ ] CHK031 - Are the no-retry policy, request-time failure outcomes, and deferred recovery behavior explicit enough to avoid conflicting resilience expectations? [Assumption, Spec §FR-017–FR-018; Plan §Concurrency, failure isolation, retries, and crash behavior]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK032 - Is the distinction between a valid empty scope and a selected scope that could not be resolved preserved in every user-facing status and error description? [Ambiguity, Spec §US1 and FR-010]
- [ ] CHK033 - Is the representation of partial scope failures sufficiently explicit for users while avoiding provider internals and fake repository rows? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, FR-010; API Contract §Execution detail additive fields]
- [ ] CHK034 - Are binary and oversized-file requirements scoped consistently with metadata-only tree processing, so file-count semantics do not imply that file contents were analyzed? [Conflict, Spec §FR-015; Plan §File policy and Repository Summary Rule]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` is a separate built-in spec-quality checklist maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add comments or findings inline; link to relevant resources or documentation.
